 K-Pop star spotted 'running with someone supporting her' at marathon.
 South Korean singer Choi Minho, a member of the popular K-pop group SHINee, had to publicly apologize after a video showing him being helped and pushed from behind by a runner at a Seoul marathon caused a huge controversy.
 Báo Tuổi Trẻ • 04/11/2026 Follow Vietnam.vn on G o o g l e Add Vietnam.vn on G o o g l e 0 Korean pop star apologizes for outrageous behavior at running event - Photo: X
 On November 3rd, Choi Minho posted an apology on his personal Instagram account, acknowledging his shortcomings during his participation in the JTBC Seoul Marathon 2026, which took place two days earlier.
 "I apologize for disappointing so many people. Everything that happened stemmed from my own shortcomings. As a sports lover, I feel extremely ashamed," Minho wrote.
 The 34-year-old singer also stated that he does not acknowledge his recent achievement and promised to be more careful in future competitions.
 The incident stemmed from the JTBC Seoul Marathon held on November 1st, where Minho attempted his first full marathon of 42.195km.
 He completed the race in 3 hours, 00 minutes, and 18 seconds, just 18 seconds slower than the sub-3 mark (completing a marathon under 3 hours), a feat many amateur runners aspire to.
 You may also like After crossing the finish line, Minho excitedly showed off his race completion certificate on social media. He admitted to regretting missing the sub-3 goal by a hair's breadth but considered it a valuable experience, and expressed his determination to conquer this milestone in his next race.
 However, the joy quickly turned into controversy when some images documenting the events on the race course circulated from November 2nd to 11th.
 In the photo, a man running alongside Minho is seen repeatedly placing his hands on the singer's back and waist, in a gesture that appears to be supporting or pushing him forward.
 Many believe this person acted as a pacer, helping runners maintain their speed. However, using their hands to push to assist movement is suspected of exceeding the permitted limits.
 According to The Korea Herald , World Athletics regulations prohibit athletes from receiving physical assistance to generate forward propulsion, except in cases of helping someone who has fallen to their feet. 
 The image shows Minho being assisted by someone - Photo: X
 Violations of the rules may result in disqualification without prior warning.
 You may also like Public opinion in South Korea is divided. Some argue that Minho only participated as an amateur runner, so there's no need to be overly strict. Conversely, many emphasize that fairness must be ensured at an official marathon, regardless of whether the participant is a professional athlete or a celebrity.
 As of November 3rd, the JTBC Seoul Marathon organizers had not yet announced an official conclusion regarding whether Minho violated any regulations. The decision to invalidate his achievement is currently only the singer's personal decision.
 Minho, born in 1991, debuted with SHINee in 2008. He is known for his passion for sports and frequently participates in endurance activities. Prior to this marathon, he finished third in the men's 35-39 age group at a triathlon in Tongyeong on October 24th.
